title: LORD, WHY HAVE YOU BROUGHT TROUBLE?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses returned to the Lord and said, "Why, Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Is this why you sent me? Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and you have not rescued your people at all."" - Exodus 5:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with Moses arguing with God. His words are raw: why have you brought trouble? Is this why you sent me? You have not rescued your people at all.

Note carefully what he does with his confusion. He returns to the Lord. He does not walk away, resign the calling, or quietly go back to Midian. He takes his complaint straight to God.

This is one of the healthiest things in the chapter. Scripture is full of such prayers — Habakkuk asking how long, David asking why God seems far away, Jesus Himself crying out on the cross with a question from Psalm 22 (Mt 27:46).

God is not fragile. He is not offended by an honest question from a hurting servant. What damages us is not the questioning; it is the silence of walking away.

And note the timing. Moses says God has not rescued them at all — and he is about to be proved gloriously wrong. Chapter 6 opens with God saying, now you will see what I will do. God's answer was already on the way while Moses was still complaining.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I taking my honest questions to God, or away from Him?
2. What am I concluding about God's inaction that may simply be too early to judge?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not understand what You are doing, and I bring that honestly to You. Hold me while I wait for Your answer. Amen.
